newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister appeals to truckers to end strike.
newsitem.headline: French minister appeals to truckers to end strike.

text.p: French Transport Minister Bernard Pons appealed again to striking truck drivers on Thursday to lift their roadblocks and return to work, saying almost all of their demands had been met.

"Perhaps the truckers don't have a good perception of reality. In a compromise, you can't get everything you want," Pons told a news conference as reports came in from across France of drivers voting to continue their 11-day-old action after negotiations with employers collapsed overnight over pay.
Pons ruled out the use of force to clear some 240 roadblocks on highways, at ports, borders, refineries and fuel depots around the provinces, which are strangling the French economy.
He was speaking after briefing conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe on the dispute after a government mediator ended his mission during the night, claiming success.

The truckers have won the right to retire at 55 instead of 60 after 25 years at the wheel and some concessions on working time and sick pay. But employers have only offered a one percent wage rise and a one-off bonus payment in response to their key demand for a pay increase of 23 percent on average.
Secretary of state for transport Anne-Marie Idrac told France 2 television that unions and bosses could continue wage negotiations now that the mediator had ended his mission.
